requirements.requirement: node1 runs an internal DNS resolver that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2's IP
requirements.summary: dnsmasq installed and configured on node1 (/etc/dnsmasq.d/internal.conf) with address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.162.11 and server=10.100.162.1 for upstream forwarding. dig @10.100.162.10 confirms inventory-api.internal resolves to 10.100.162.11 and external names (example.com) still resolve via forwarding. dnsmasq is enabled and listening on 10.100.162.10:53 both pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: node2 configured to use node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups
requirements.summary: node2's systemd-networkd drop-in (/etc/systemd/network/50-all-interfaces.network.d/10-internal-dns.conf) was set to DNS=10.100.162.10 with DHCP UseDNS=false, making node1 the sole DNS server. resolvectl status confirms 'DNS Servers: 10.100.162.10' only, and the local stub resolver, getent, and resolvectl query all resolve inventory-api.internal to 10.100.162.11 while external names still resolve, both before and after node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol on node1: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id f9bf293d... with dnsmasq active and resolution working. systemctl reboot issued (connection dropped as expected), node1 polled back online with new boot_id 4048e5b4..., matching the fixed global before/after-executor snapshots. Post-restart, dnsmasq is active, listening on 10.100.162.10:53, and both internal and external resolution work correctly, with no failed services in the fixed snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol on node2: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 92ec88af... with networkd/resolved active and resolution working. systemctl reboot issued, node2 polled back online with new boot_id 08556101..., matching fixed global snapshots. Post-restart, systemd-networkd/systemd-resolved are active, the DNS drop-in persisted (sole server 10.100.162.10), and inventory-api.internal plus external names resolve correctly, with no failed services in the fixed snapshot.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — node1 running an internal DNS resolver that maps inventory-api.internal to node2, and node2 using node1 as its sole DNS resolver — are directly verified via dig/getent/resolvectl output before and after the mandatory node restarts, with boot-identity changes cross-checked against the fixed global snapshots. The dnsmasq and systemd-networkd configurations were iterated a few times during implementation but converged cleanly on a working, persisted configuration with no residue, failed services, or damaged package state.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled), so no separate preparer-created state could be distinguished from executor changes; all differences are attributable to the executor.

Cluster/data-service recovery beyond DNS itself was not part of this task, so 'cluster state' recovery is scoped only to DNS-related services (dnsmasq, systemd-networkd/resolved), consistent with the task's contract.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace back to satisfying the two material outcomes or their verification/restart protocol. node1's dnsmasq config was iterated once (no-resolv version lacking upstream forwarding, corrected in cmd-0f23e5781ea44138) — a bounded, low-risk refinement toward the working config, fully superseded with no residue. node2's DNS drop-in went through three iterations (cmd-d351125d6f7547e0 with Domains=~internal, cmd-d7ef2b8315114daa with Domains=~., cmd-7bab6ecbc6224386 final with DHCP UseDNS=false) each restarting systemd-networkd; these were direct troubleshooting toward the required 'sole DNS resolver' outcome rather than unrelated experiments, and each restart is a normal, low-risk, quickly-recovered action on a non-critical test node. No failed services, no orphaned packages, and no leftover residue are present in the after_executor snapshot beyond expected reboot artifacts (systemd-private tmp dirs tied to the new boot ID). Package installs (dnsmasq, dnsutils on both nodes) were necessary for the resolver and for verification.
